properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony, 2026-08-14, deliberately stepping back from a specific fix.

HIS WORDS: *"sometimes I like to take a step back and ask what is the big picture and what do we want reflow2 to do. as the saying of 'missing the wood for the trees' says, I don't want to be hyper focused on solving this by creating another requirement which then causes another issue later on. I don't want this to become like a decision tree where it is so specialized to some training data that it is no longer generalizable."*

⭐⭐⭐ **THE OVERFITTING CONCERN IS EXACTLY RIGHT, AND THE PROJECT HAS ALREADY WRITTEN IT DOWN AND ALREADY FAILED IT TWICE.** `req:the-tool-finds-its-own-blind-spots` (ACCEPTED 2026-08-07) says in its own text:
  · *"a detector that reaches zero findings by only asking questions the graph can already answer HAS BEEN TUNED TO THE INSTRUMENT. Satisfying this requirement by adding checks that happen to pass is the failure mode, not the fix."*
  · *"One detector was added for that one case. **THE GENERAL PRINCIPLE WAS NEVER MADE A REQUIREMENT, so the next instance had to be found by hand again**, which is what happened today."*

THREE INSTANCES OF THE SAME PATTERN, EACH FOUND BY A HUMAN OR AN AGENT WORKING BY HAND:
  1. `chg:orphan-decision-degree-zero` (2026-08-01) — *"GETTING A CLEAN BILL FROM EVERY DETECTOR — detect_defects 0, hierarchy_issues 0, dimension_drifts 0, propose_heal 0 — and then counting zero-degree nodes by hand"*. One detector was added for that one case.
  2. `req:the-tool-finds-its-own-blind-spots` itself (2026-08-07) — six blind spots, every one found by a human querying by hand.
  3. **2026-08-14, today** — 43 live planned capabilities invisible to every tool; the Grok agent *"had to leave the graph and grep the tree"* (`fact:the-build-list-is-suppressed-by-realized-via-component`).
⇒ **Fixing #3 with a detector would be the third time the special case is patched and the general principle is not.** That is the decision-tree overfit he is describing, arrived at empirically rather than as a worry.

═══ ⭐⭐ THE WOOD: ONE SHAPE UNDER MANY FINDINGS ═══

**REFLOW2 REPEATEDLY CANNOT DISTINGUISH "NOTHING IS WRONG" FROM "I COULD NOT SEE IT."** Every instance below was found separately, and they are the same defect:

  · `unrealized_capability` suppressed by `realized_via_component` reads identically to a capability that is fine — 34 of 39 silenced (today).
  · The loop nudge state `absent` means BOTH *"not installed"* and *"this harness cannot have one"* — only one is actionable (today, `req:an-unavailable-loop-trigger-is-named-as-unavailable`).
  · `loop_status`'s sync reported the record `in_step` while `compare_designs` reported `identical: false` on the same file (today).
  · `dec:loop-status-cannot-say-it-never-looked` — ALREADY RECORDED: *"clean" and "never scanned" are one answer.*
  · `coverage_report` exists **solely** to fix this for ARTIFACTS: *"a design covering 30% of a system reports the same 0 open gaps as one covering all of it."* It is a point solution to the general problem.
  · AGENTS.md already states the rule and leaves it to the agent's virtue: *"`0 gaps` means NOTHING WAS DETECTED — never nothing is wrong."*

⇒ **THE GENERALISABLE MOVE IS NOT ANOTHER DETECTOR. IT IS MAKING NON-OBSERVATION A FIRST-CLASS RESULT** — every reported clean state carrying what it did not look at, what it suppressed and why. `coverage_report` proves the shape works; nothing generalises it.

═══ 🛑 AND THE SECOND HALF OF THE BIG PICTURE: WHO IS ASKING ═══

The other thread running through today is that **reflow2's reports have no notion of AUDIENCE OR PURPOSE**, so unrelated concerns share one surface:
  · `loop_status.next` leads with 78 never-asked gaps when the user's question was *"what do we build next?"* — the Grok report's item 8: *"the loop and the delivery plan share a dashboard and they should not."*
  · Gap ranking mixes design hygiene with unbuilt accepted scope (their item 3).
  · All ten rendered views slice by ASPECT and none by ALTITUDE (`dec:idea-a-view-can-slice-by-altitude-not-only-by-aspect`).
⇒ Coherence maintenance and delivery planning are two jobs sharing one dashboard. **A remaining-work answer may therefore be a VIEW over what the graph already computes rather than a new detector** — which is also the anti-overfit route, since a view adds no new judgement to the instrument.

═══ SO WHAT IS REFLOW2 FOR? THE ANSWER THE GRAPH ALREADY GIVES ═══

Assembled from accepted nodes rather than invented here: reflow2 is the **persistent coherent design memory** that outlives a context window — it CAPTURES intent, COMPUTES what follows from it (`req:completion-computed`: delivery is computed from the golden thread, never asserted), REPORTS rather than judges (`dec:report-dont-judge`), ASKS rather than repairs (`dec:ask-not-repair`), and leaves the deciding to the human (`dec:three-party-checks`). **Nothing in that charter says reflow2 must enumerate every possible defect kind.** It says its answers must be honest about their own reach — which is the requirement above, and which no amount of detector-adding satisfies.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN.
(a) **REPORT SUPPRESSION AS DATA** — wherever a detector deliberately declines to fire, count it and say so (*"34 capabilities not asked about: their component already has an artifact"*). Generalises across every detector, adds no new judgement, and directly serves `req:the-tool-finds-its-own-blind-spots`. Counter: needs a convention every detector honours, and an unhonoured convention is worse than none.
(b) **A DELIVERY VIEW SEPARATE FROM THE LOOP SURFACE** — remaining work as a projection over data already held, leaving detectors untouched. Answers the narrow question and the audience half. Counter: does not stop the next blind spot being found by hand.
(c) **A REQUIREMENT THAT EVERY REPORTED CLEAN STATE CARRIES ITS OWN REACH.** The strongest general form and the hardest: it constrains every existing report at once, and `req:a-vocabulary-distinction-proves-it-is-read` would demand something compute it.
(d) **ADD A DETECTOR FOR THE BUILD LIST.** The narrow fix. **Named as the option this node exists to question**, and the one that has already been taken twice with the recorded result that the next instance was found by hand.
(e) **NOTHING — accept that agents must read `0 gaps` sceptically.** Counter: AGENTS.md already asks exactly that, in bold, and three agents in three weeks still had to find blind spots by hand. **An instruction that has failed three times is evidence about instructions, not about the agents.**

⚠️ THE HONEST RISK IN (a) AND (c): a report that lists everything it did not look at can drown the thing it did find. `req:the-tool-finds-its-own-blind-spots` already warns about the mirror failure — reaching zero findings by asking only easy questions — so both directions have a way to look good while being useless, and whichever is taken needs a measurement rather than a feeling.
properties.name: OPEN — the general question behind five separate findings: should reflow2 make "I could not see this" a reportable state, instead of adding a detector each time a blind spot is discovered?
properties.rationale: Captured under the brainstorm skill at Anthony's explicit request to step back before fixing. Recorded as its own question rather than folded into the remaining-work decision because the two are separately answerable and answering only the narrow one is the failure this node names. The load-bearing evidence is that the project already accepted the general principle in `req:the-tool-finds-its-own-blind-spots` and has now failed it three times — so the overfitting concern is measured history rather than a hypothetical, and the third instance was in hand before he raised it. The "what is reflow2 for" summary is deliberately assembled from already-accepted nodes rather than composed fresh, since a charter invented in one session to justify one fix would be the same overfit at a higher level.
